problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14014428/assets/c4f2a9119ff41c5f9b34575c26f3df626df9f2db6d55bb3bc4f5709598055c82.png)

Consider the graph of $y=f(x)$ above. Which of the following statements is true?
worked_solution:
From the graph, we see that

- The slope of the tangent at $x=2$ is zero, so ${f}^{′}(2)=0.$

- The slope of the tangent at $x=3$ is negative, so ${f}^{′}(3)<0.$

- The slope of the tangent at $x=6$ is positive, so ${f}^{′}(6)>0.$

Therefore, ${f}^{′}(3)<{f}^{′}(2)<{f}^{′}(6).$

Question 16
?

Consider the graph of y=f(x) above. Which of the following statements is true?

a
f′(3)<f′(6)<f′(2)
b
f′(2)<f′(3)<f′(6)
c
f′(2)<f′(6)<f′(3)
d
f′(6)<f′(2)<f′(3)
e
f′(3)<f′(2)<f′(6)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

From the graph, we see that

  • The slope of the tangent at x=2 is zero, so f′(2)=0.

  • The slope of the tangent at x=3 is negative, so f′(3)<0.

  • The slope of the tangent at x=6 is positive, so f′(6)>0.

Therefore, f′(3)<f′(2)<f′(6).
